subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Early stage and locally advanced NSCLC: surgery, chemoradiation and adjuvant or perioperative therapy

steps.tx: Early stage and locally advanced **non-small cell lung cancer** (NSCLC) is usually treated with curative intent. Surgical resection is the cornerstone for resectable disease. **Lobectomy** with mediastinal nodal assessment is the standard operation, because it gives better local control than sublobar resection in most fit patients. Sublobar resection is reserved for patients with poor lung reserve or small peripheral tumours. Patient fitness and pulmonary function guide the choice.

rows: Central tumours not amenable to lobectomy

steps.tx: Surgical approach matters. **Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery** (VATS) lobectomy is preferred for early disease when feasible. Tumours above about 6 cm, or with significant bronchial involvement, often need open thoracotomy. Uniportal and robotic approaches are alternatives in experienced centres. A utility incision should be under 8 cm and avoid rib spreading, as per standard VATS definitions. Indian practice often uses open surgery more widely because of resource constraints.

nodes.label: Tumour under 6 cm, no major bronchial involvement

steps.tx: Neoadjuvant and perioperative **immunotherapy** can be considered for resectable disease without **driver mutations**, typically stage II to IIIB. Pre-operative **platinum chemotherapy** combined with a PD-1 inhibitor improved pathological response and event-free outcomes. Pembrolizumab given both before and after surgery improved event-free and overall survival. Many guidelines now list these approaches, but cost limits access in India, so careful patient selection matters.

left.title: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy
points: PD-1 inhibitor plus platinum before surgery

steps.tx: For unresectable stage III disease, **concurrent chemoradiation** is the standard approach, with radiotherapy delivered alongside platinum-based chemotherapy. In patients who have not progressed after chemoradiation, **consolidative anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy** for up to one year improved progression-free and overall survival in the PACIFIC trial. For medically inoperable stage I tumours, **stereotactic body radiotherapy** (SBRT) is the preferred ablative option, giving high local control in peripheral lesions.
